encounters.cc: History of intense relationships that alternate between idealization and devaluation

lines: History of intense relationships that alternate between idealization and devaluation
She reports a persistent fear of abandonment and admits to engaging in self-harm when feeling distressed.
She also describes chronic feelings of emptiness and has had several episodes of intense anger that she finds difficult to control.
She has been in psychotherapy for the past year with minimal improvement in her symptoms.
Her medical history is significant for major depressive disorder and recurrent urinary tract infections.
Her current medications include sertraline and an oral contraceptive.

encounters.cc: Weakness and palpitations for the past two months

lines: Weakness and palpitations for the past two months
She has a past medical history of depression and an eating disorder, for which she is currently not receiving treatment.
She denies the use of medications, laxatives, or diuretics.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time administrative assistant.
Her blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, heart rate is 88 bpm
She appears thin but otherwise well
- Urine chloride: 15 mEq/L (Normal: 110-250 mEq/L on a normal diet)

encounters.cc: Superficial laceration on her left forearm after argument with boyfriend

lines: Superficial laceration on her left forearm after argument with boyfriend
24-year-old female with prior evaluation for intense interpersonal relationships and weakness with palpitations who presents with a superficial laceration.
She reports cutting herself during an argument with her boyfriend, stating it was the only way to cope with her overwhelming emotions.
She has a history of similar episodes in the past, often triggered by interpersonal conflicts.
She also mentions periods of intense anger, during which she has broken objects and shouted at loved ones.
She admits to occasional auditory hallucinations during periods of extreme stress, which resolve without intervention.
Her relationships are described as intense but unstable, with a pattern of idealization and devaluation.
On examination, you notice several older, healed scars on both forearms.
She appears anxious and her mood fluctuates during the interview.
- Comprehensive metabolic panel: within normal limits
- Thyroid function tests: within normal limits

encounters.cc: Self-inflicted lacerations on forearm brought by roommate

lines: Self-inflicted lacerations on forearm brought by roommate
The patient returns to the emergency department six months after her prior presentation for superficial laceration, presenting with self-inflicted lacerations.
She has a history of intense relationships with frequent conflicts, and she reports feeling empty and fears abandonment.
She has had multiple emergency department visits for self-harm and suicidal ideation but has never attempted suicide.
During her hospital stay, she alternately praises and devalues different members of the healthcare team, stating that some are the only ones who understand her while others are trying to harm her.
She has no other medical history.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time administrative assistant.
Her temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, and respirations are 16/min.
Physical examination shows superficial lacerations on her forearms and no other abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Found drowsy and confused by roommate with empty bottle of sertraline

lines: Found drowsy and confused by roommate with empty bottle of sertraline

This 25-year-old female with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and bulimia nervosa, who has presented previously for self-inflicted lacerations, is brought to the emergency department.
The roommate mentions finding an empty bottle of sertraline next to her.
The patient has a history of depression.
She has been prescribed sertraline, which she started taking 3 weeks ago.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time administrative assistant.
A heart rate of 110 bpm, blood pressure of 130/85 mmHg, and a respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute.
On examination, the patient is somnolent but arousable, with
She has dilated pupils and dry mucous membranes.

encounters.cc: Ingestion of extra-strength acetaminophen in suicide attempt approximately 2 hours ago

lines: Ingestion of extra-strength acetaminophen in suicide attempt approximately 2 hours ago

The patient is a 26-year-old female with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and bulimia nervosa, with prior ED visits for self-harm and overdose, who presents following acetaminophen ingestion.
She is currently asymptomatic but expresses regret about her actions.
She is unable to provide an exact amount of acetaminophen ingested but indicates that she took "a handful" of 500 mg tablets.
Her roommate found an empty bottle that originally contained 50 tablets.
She has a history of depression.
She has been taking sertraline for the past year.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time administrative assistant.
Her vital signs are within normal limits
Physical examination is unremarkable. The patient is alert and oriented
Initial laboratory studies are ordered, including a complete blood count, liver function tests, and serum acetaminophen level.
The patient's serum acetaminophen level returns at 150 mcg/mL, drawn 2 hours post-ingestion.

encounters.cc: Confused and agitated at home, suspected medication overdose

lines: Confused and agitated at home, suspected medication overdose

The patient with borderline personality disorder returns following prior emergency department visits for self-harm and medication overdose, and is brought to the emergency department by her friends after they found her confused and agitated at home.
They report that she has been depressed recently and suspect she may have taken an overdose of her medication.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time administrative assistant.
Heart rate of 120 beats per minute. Her blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg.
On examination, the patient is tachycardic, has dilated pupils, dry skin, and is intermittently seizing.
An ECG shows a QRS duration of 120 msec and occasional ventricular ectopic beats.

encounters.cc: Unresponsive at home next to empty pill bottle labeled amitriptyline

lines: Unresponsive at home next to empty pill bottle labeled amitriptyline
The patient is a 27-year-old woman with borderline personality disorder and multiple prior overdoses, including a tricyclic antidepressant overdose four months ago.
She is brought to the emergency department by her friends after they found her unresponsive at home next to an empty pill bottle labeled 'amitriptyline.'
Her medical history is significant for major depressive disorder.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time administrative assistant.
On examination, her temperature is 39.1°C (102.4°F), blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, and respirations are 22/min.
She is drowsy but arousable. Her pupils are dilated and bowel sounds are diminished.
An ECG shows a QRS interval of 120 ms.
